beats: Status: blocked in the syllabus (no deck; the speaker's OK is pending). Planned from the recording (course/L15.transcript.md) so a narration-only cut with our own drawings is ready if the user approves; no voice clips, no slides.
Hook: the CUDA programming guide grew from about 100 pages (CUDA 2.2, when the speaker learned it) to over 600 (line_gluon_manual_tower).

Threads vs tiles: a warp moves in lockstep anyway, so program the group, not each thread (L09-04's line_tiles_megaphone / line_tiles_tray_handoff and L09-01's line_gpu_squad_march from the library); a tile is one piece of the puzzle (line_gluon_jigsaw_hands; Triton Puzzles is the beginner's way in).

What Triton hides inside the block: memory coalescing, bank conflicts, tensor-core layouts, caching, pipelining (L09-04's line_tiles_meal_kit); JIT: compile on first use, then load the cached binary (reuse line_card_catalog).

Layout, the key idea of Gluon: the mapping from a tile's elements to threads, warps and memory, a seating plan (line_gluon_seating_plan); swizzling staggers the rows so neighbours do not collide in one memory bank (line_gluon_brick_stagger); linear layouts replace tens of hand-written layouts and about 100 conversion functions with one rule.

Gluon: one level below Triton; you choose the layouts and give each warp group one job (load, matrix math, epilogue, scheduler): warp specialization (line_gluon_brigade_roles); manual vs automatic (line_gluon_two_levers); near the vendor library's matmul speed with a single configuration.

Which to use: Triton for most memory-bound kernels (softmax, layer norm); Gluon when the kernel has a dot product on the newest GPUs. The real question is who steers, the programmer or the compiler (line_gluon_dual_control_car).

The future: one magic compiler that does it all was too optimistic (L09-04's line_tiles_bread_machine); lightweight languages built for each chip (line_gluon_multitool_vs_set); LLMs write kernels faster than people can review them (line_gluon_printer_flood).
Closing, the speaker's answer to "which one wins": none of them; the future will be invented by the students (line_gluon_students_blueprint).

Cover (line_cover_l15_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): a driving-school car seen through the windscreen: the learner grips the wheel, the instructor's foot hovers over her own brake.
